It deliberately shows the client-rendered-shell case: one root cause suppresses ~19 downstream checks, so the report carries ONE critical finding instead of a dozen false positives, two category scores are null (not zero), and `coverage` of 0.23 signals that the 85 headline rests on a small slice of the audit.

findings.title: Meaningful content exists without JavaScript
findings.plain_summary: Your content is built by the browser, so AI assistants that do not run JavaScript see an empty page.
findings.signal: Visible text length in the raw (pre-JavaScript) HTML response
findings.evidence:
Raw HTML body contained a single
and 0 characters of visible text; the rendered DOM added 1,912 characters of product facts.
findings.impact: Crawlers that do not execute JavaScript see an empty shell. Every fact on this page is invisible to them, so nothing is quotable or citable, and 19 downstream checks could not be evaluated at all.

suggested_action.summary: Server-render or pre-render the homepage so key facts are present in the initial HTML response.
suggested_action.snippet:
// Next.js: export async function getServerSideProps() { ... }
// or statically pre-render at build time with getStaticProps()
suggested_action.validation: Run: curl -s https://example.com/ | grep -i "<your product fact>" — the fact must appear without executing JavaScript.

recommendations.title: Anchor your identity to an authority node
recommendations.summary: Once structured data is reachable, add at least one sameAs link pointing to an authority such as Wikidata or Crunchbase.
recommendations.rationale: Valid markup that only links to your own properties leaves the corroboration chain unanchored, so entity confusion persists even though the schema itself is correct. This is not flagged as a defect because structured data could not be evaluated on this scan.
recommendations.validation: Paste the page into Google's Rich Results Test and confirm the Organization entity lists the authority URL.
